history_findings.finding: The 2026-02-25 Project-Frankenstein adaptive vision design used an explicit two-stage routing policy: a fast detector/OCR pipeline first, then a local VLM only when heuristic confidence fell below 0.55 or question/scene triggers demanded deeper understanding.
history_findings.caveat: The code comment that roughly 90% of images avoid VLM is a design/runtime claim in source code, not a verified Level-0 benchmark receipt.

history_findings.finding: On 2026-03-19 the architecture deliberately removed tools/frank_visual_pipeline.py, tools/frank_adaptive_vision.py and the prior VCB vision bridge, replacing them with one CPU-only tools/frank_eye.py path. This was a real simplification/supersession, not merely a rename.

Unified FrankEye combined Digital Retina v8 CNN classification, DINOv2 scene features, GOLPU/GoL texture features, Tesseract OCR and OpenCV face analysis into a low-latency CPU pipeline. The current frozen-head file still labels the Retina CNN path 'inference only'.

By 2026-03-24 Project-Frankenstein explicitly removed CIFAR-10 classification from screenshot analysis because it produced useless output; screenshot handling was specialized toward app/browser context and OCR preprocessing. This is a concrete modality-mismatch negative result.

cross_source_reconciliation.finding: The Drive Digital Retina lineage contains learned GoL dictionary/prototype and replay/calibration mechanisms that are richer as adaptive-learning ancestors than the current Project-Frankenstein FrankEye path. Those learning mechanisms did not survive as online/user-specific learning inside current FrankEye; current FrankEye preserves sensor/feature infrastructure but not the historical learned-dictionary behavior as an adaptive authority layer.

Project-Frankenstein contributes a separate routing lesson: first-stage cheap evidence plus conditional escalation is historically validated as an architecture pattern, while Drive Retina contributes prototype/dictionary learning and realistic-negative calibration. The current Clay v0.1 target should treat these as complementary ancestors rather than one continuous implementation.

negative_results_and_failure_modes: Generic CIFAR-10 screenshot labels were explicitly removed as useless; image modality must influence classifier/readout selection.
Heuristic escalation confidence in the old adaptive pipeline was hand-coded and question-sensitive; it is not equivalent to calibrated open-set familiarity or semantic correctness.
Current FrankEye's Digital Retina CNN is inference-only and uses narrow CIFAR classes; it cannot satisfy the current user-specific adaptive Micro Visual Classifier contract by itself.
Architecture unification can silently discard useful historical learning mechanisms even while retaining the same 'Retina' naming; lineage must be mechanism-based, not name-based.

reuse: Keep FrankEye-like dissolved sensor/feature extraction as a low-latency CPU evidence plane.
Reuse selective escalation/routing as a policy pattern, but calibrate it against measured cost and uncertainty rather than fixed hand-coded confidence alone.
Add the adaptive Micro Visual Classifier as a versioned, user-scoped, non-authoritative familiarity/readout layer over frozen reusable features; do not pretend current FrankEye already learns online.
Preserve modality-specific readout branches so screenshots can bypass or downweight object classifiers proven unhelpful there.
Differentially test DINO/CLIP-like embeddings versus historical GoL signatures for recurring user-specific classes and realistic OOD negatives.
do_not_reuse_as_authority: Old 0.55 heuristic escalation threshold as a calibrated open-set gate.
The source-code '~90% no VLM' comment as measured routing savings.
CIFAR classification as generic screen understanding.
Retina/FrankEye naming continuity as evidence that adaptive learning survived the refactor.
current_architecture_delta.recommended_discriminating_test: In H1, replay the same mixed photo/screenshot/user-recurring/OOD corpus through (A) current FrankEye features only, (B) FrankEye+DINO prototype MVC, and (C) historical GoL-signature prototype MVC. Preregister known-class accuracy, open-set AUROC/FPR, screenshot false-positive rate, calibration, per-update CPU/RAM/latency, forgetting and routing savings.
